In these and other similar cases elsewhere in the program, the assumed values tend toward conservative numbers, those which give higher concentration or worst-case effects. 2.2 Characterization of the dimensions and duration of the dense gas cloud To properly characterize a dense gas phase, physical parameters such as length, width, and height were needed. Based on methods in by Britter and Heavens (Britter, 1989; Havens et al, 1989), formulations were developed to account for these parameters, listed below by their formal names in the literature. • The Zone of Established Flow (S) • The Depth of the 100% Concentration Cloud (d) • The plume radius (r) 8 LLNL-TR-818768 The cloud concentrations during the dense gas phase are assumed to be 100%. Therefore, a method for calculating concentrations during this phase was unnecessary. 2.2.1 The Zone of Flow Establishment (S) The Zone of Flow Establishment (S), represents the downwind extent of the highly concentrated dense gas zone (Fig. 2.2, Eq. 2) Figure 2.2.
